propositions: A failed or timed-out tickets-branch fetch causes rebar init to silently create an empty orphan branch that diverges from an existing remote branch.
A shared tri-state remote-branch probe using git ls-remote must distinguish advertised, reachable-absent, and unreachable, consumed by all four init consumers.
On an unreachable or timing-out remote, init must fail closed with a distinct error and create no orphan unless --force-new-store is explicitly supplied.
When the remote advertises the branch but fetch fails, init must return nonzero without creating an orphan; reachable-absent still bootstraps normally.
The probe result is cached with a short TTL keyed by repo/remote/branch so one CLI invocation performs at most one probe, re-probing after clock advance.
The cold fetch retains its 300-second bound while the advertisement probe has its own short bound, both folding timeout to return code 124.
